# Frozen-evaluation scenario set (80 cases)

`scenarios.json` holds the only inputs a system under test may see. `oracle.json`
is the evaluator-only answer key. Both are synthetic and fictional, live outside
application code, catalog/Storage ingestion, prompts and traces, and must never
be imported or read by runtime modules (a unit test scans `app/`, `gas/` and
`supabase/` for any reference).

## Shape

- 80 scenarios: 40 text, 24 voice, 16 photo. 60 `development`, 20 `holdout`.
  Development is 30 text / 18 voice / 12 photo; holdout is 10 / 6 / 4.
- 20 opaque families (`G01`..`G20`) of four scenarios each. A family is one
  business situation seen through different channels or paraphrases. The split is
  made **by family** (15 development, 5 holdout) so a paraphrase or recording of
  the same request cannot sit on both sides of the boundary. Scenario and family
  ids are shuffled and reveal neither the split nor the expected outcome.
- Each scenario is one conversation: an ordered list of customer turns. A text
  turn has `text`. A voice turn has a `spec` (the script and the acoustic conditions)
  and an `asset` (`media/<scenario>-t<turn>.wav`). A photo turn has a `spec` (label text
  and capture conditions) and an `asset` (`media/<scenario>-t<turn>.png`). The 40 files
  are generated by `scripts/generate_evaluation_media.py` and hashed in `media/MANIFEST.json`.
  They are **synthetic**: Windows text-to-speech (David/Zira) with declared noise, telephone
  band, clipping, overlap and rate changes, and Pillow-drawn labels with declared glare,
  stickers, blur, fading and handwriting. They are harder than clean studio audio but are not
  human speech or camera photos; real recordings/photos remain an open gap.
- The oracle gives one checkpoint per turn (`clarify`, `needs_staff` or
  `draft_quote`, with a reason code), the final requested lines, the expected
  USD subtotal (tax excluded, no discount, no shipping), optional labeled
  retrieval targets and whether the first turn contains a consequential
  ambiguity that must be clarified or escalated.

## Why the outcomes look the way they do

They follow the product's documented policy, not a model's opinion:

- Only a complete written order (`written_requests.parse_written_request`) can
  confirm SKU and quantity. Prose, "a dozen", "boxes", alternatives, conditions,
  negation, unknown separators such as "plus", and injected instructions get a
  clarification. Audio and photos never confirm themselves, so every media turn is
  a `clarify` checkpoint (`needs_written_confirmation`). Because a model may judge any
  reading unreliable and route it to staff, every media checkpoint also lists
  `needs_staff` as an acceptable safe alternative (`also_acceptable`); a draft is never
  acceptable before a written confirmation. `exact_match` still reports primary actions.
  This rule was widened from 18 to all 40 media checkpoints after the first paid
  development run (which scored 55/60 under the narrower rule); decide such rules before
  looking at a holdout.
- A complete order whose every line is current, in stock and within observed
  availability becomes a staff-review draft. Any unknown, discontinued, out-of-stock
  or over-stock line sends the whole order to staff (`needs_staff`); no substitute
  is chosen.
- Subtotals and line support are verified by `scripts/evaluation_dataset.py`
  from an independent restatement of the seeded catalog, not copied from the system.

## What this set does not prove

- Authoring `oracle.json` from the policy means a baseline that implements the
  policy will score highly **by construction**. A pass shows internal consistency
  and regression safety, not agent quality, speech recognition, label reading or
  retrieval recall on real noisy input.
- Retrieval-labeled cases are few: 4 development (2 text, 1 voice, 1 photo) and 3
  holdout (1 each). The offline baseline can only run the 2 development text ones.
  Neither count is a statistically meaningful recall estimate.
- Final outcomes are 31 draft / 18 staff / 11 clarify in development and
  13 draft / 4 staff / 3 clarify in holdout. The holdout escalation denominator
  (4) is small, so a zero-unsupported-line result there is weak evidence.
- The same author wrote development and holdout cases in one session, and the
  holdout answers are visible in this repository. Keep them out of prompt, code and
  threshold tuning. If a holdout result drives any change, that holdout is spent and
  a new reserved set is required (`docs/TESTING_PLAN.md` section 9).
- No holdout run has been made, and both runners refuse to select it.
- The first paid agent run (development only, 60 scenarios, run 1 of 1) scored 59/60 under the
  final rule (53/60 exact primary action). Its single failure is a model flake on "1 OD-001"
  (quantity read as unknown). It also exposed a null-SKU placeholder bug in candidate discovery,
  fixed afterwards and not re-measured because paid calls were stopped. See
  `docs/evidence/evaluation-development-agent-2026-11-02.json`. These numbers are development
  results on synthetic assets, not holdout, human-speech or client results.

## Commands

```
node scripts/python.cjs -m pytest tests/unit/test_evaluation_dataset.py -q
node scripts/python.cjs scripts/evaluate_scenarios.py --company <synthetic company uuid> --output <evidence json>
```

The first validates structure and catalog consistency. The second needs local
Supabase and runs only the 30 development text scenarios against the offline
exact-order baseline, writing counts by modality with run / not-run denominators.
